title: The Educated Barbarian: Meditations analysis (part. 15)
summary: Part 15 of NH's Meditations series, halfway through the book. Themes: the soul must not quit while the body holds out (his favourite quote), avoiding the arrogance of 'Caesarism', balancing selfishness and selflessness, emulating Antoninus selectively, stepping back from problems as from a dream, rejecting hedonism and excess comfort, and the interconnection of knowledge.
claims: His favourite quote: it's a dishonour for the soul to give up while the body still holds out
The body is resilient and can always recover; staying injury-free or healing starts with the mind wanting it
A strong body creates a strong soul and vice versa; if the spirit weakens the body follows
Your body is a gift from the source, your parents and ancestors; respect and use it
Feeling superior once you gain wisdom takes you off the stoic path; wisdom should make you a guide who brings others up
Negative people are loudest; most people are neutral and worth your time and effort
He is deeply selfish but balances it with total selflessness elsewhere; keeping some selfishness lets you reach your potential
Don't copy a role model entirely; pick traits from the list and study them
Fear never made him better; fear is created in your head so you can destroy it
Apply stoic virtues step by step, not all at once
Problems look huge up close; step back and treat them like a nightmare you wake from, then work on them with a clear mind
Hedonism, pursuing pleasure for its own sake, is shared with tyrants and criminals; taken to its end it leads to obesity, disease and overdose
Enjoy earthly pleasures but never let them control you; don't eat a favourite treat every week or make it a habit
Too much comfort makes you soft; comfort is good only to the degree it preserves health and recovery
Each concept you learn opens many more; read enough books and you'll already know part of any new one
Forgetting who you are and your roots disconnects you from the world
